concepts.label: Query Link API (Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - covers all three GET read variants this page documents at different filter granularities against the identical Links response schema: GET /analytics/link (all scopes), GET /analytics/link/{scope} (one scope), GET /analytics/link/{scope}/{name} (one link). Kept as one concept rather than three near-duplicates per this round's 'let a reference table be a reference table' guidance - they are the same read operation, not three distinct mechanisms.

concepts.label: Create Link API (Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - POST /analytics/link/{scope}/{name}, first contact. Checked against analytics:create-analytics-scope/create-analytics-collection/create-analytics-synonym/create-analytics-index (round 21's 5_ddl.md CREATE statement family) and against candidate-evidence.py for analytics:create-link-statement (no match) - Analytics has no SQL++ CREATE LINK DDL statement at all; link creation is REST/UI/CLI-only, genuinely distinct from the CONNECT LINK/DISCONNECT LINK DDL statements which toggle an EXISTING link's ingestion state rather than defining a new one.

concepts.label: Edit Link API (Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - PUT /analytics/link/{scope}/{name}, first contact. Cannot change the link's name, type, or scope - only its connection/credential parameters.

concepts.label: Delete Link API (Analytics)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - DELETE /analytics/link/{scope}/{name}, first contact. Fails if any Analytics collection or other entity still uses the link.

concepts.label: Legacy Link API (Analytics, deprecated)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the three deprecated flat-path operations (DELETE/POST/PUT /analytics/link, using a dataverse+name form/query parameter pair instead of a /{scope}/{name} path) grouped as one concept since the page itself groups them under one 'Legacy Methods' heading and states the identical deprecation/backward-compatibility rationale for all three.

concepts.label: Analytics link type enum (couchbase/s3/azureblob/gcs)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - checked candidate-evidence.py, no existing analytics:link-type-enum. The closed choice of remote-data-source kind a link can be created as; 'couchbase' maps to the already-promoted analytics:remote-link, and 's3'/'azureblob'/'gcs' each map to analytics:external-link's three documented external-source variants. Notably has no 'local' value at all - Local links cannot be created, edited, or (per the Query All Links default) even listed through this enum, a third independent confirmation of round 21's 'uniquely uneditable and undeletable' finding for the promoted analytics:local-link.

notable_absence.finding: This page's create/edit/delete/query operations manage a link's DEFINITION (credentials, type, host) but never mention CONNECT LINK or DISCONNECT LINK at all - the DDL statements (round 21, analytics:connect-link-statement/disconnect-link-statement) that start/stop a link's ingestion state have no REST equivalent documented on this page, and this page has no equivalent of those two statements either. The two REST/DDL surfaces are complementary (define-the-link vs toggle-its-ingestion), never overlapping, and no page anywhere in the corpus states an equivalence between them - confirmed absent rather than assumed.

cross_component_finding: This page is the first-hand REST source for facts round 21's manage-links.json (a UI task page) had recorded with IDENTICAL wording but only reached via seeAlso cross-reference: the mgmt/mgmtSSL/kv/kvSSL port requirements for remote links, and the encryption-mode choice. It also independently confirms, at a third point in the corpus (UI, DDL, and now REST), that a Local link is uniquely excluded from every general-purpose link-management surface: it has no type-enum value here, and the Query All Links endpoint explicitly excludes it by default.
cross_product_finding: None found on this page - all link management is Analytics-Service-internal REST with no stated Capella or cross-product parallel, though the S3/Azure Blob/GCS external-link credential parameter families (accessKeyId/secretAccessKey, accountKey/sharedAccessSignature, jsonCredentials/applicationDefaultCredentials) closely mirror generic cloud-provider auth patterns documented elsewhere in the corpus for backup/restore cloud targets - no page states an explicit equivalence, so this is an observation, not a minted relation.
